summary: Establishes normative script policy: POSIX shell by default; PowerShell only when Windows support is explicit
migration_impact: Authoring policy is POSIX shell by default and PowerShell only when Windows support is explicit. import-payload and bootstrap --apply still copy every manifest script, including .ps1. Default projects delete scripts/*.ps1 and scripts/plate/*.ps1 after scaffold. Import-time filtering is #1019.
migration_guidance: 1. Review platform stance: default projects (no explicit Windows support) author .sh only; explicit Windows support = dual-stack (.sh + .ps1); Windows-only = .ps1 only.
2. Scaffold still copies .ps1. Workaround until #1019: after import or bootstrap --apply, delete scripts/*.ps1 and scripts/plate/*.ps1 when Windows support was not declared.
3. When creating new scripts, check declared platform support first. Do not wait for an explicit POSIX statement: no Windows declaration means .sh only.
4. Platform support must come from human-stated project intent (SPEC.md, .plate config, onboarding answers, explicit instruction) — never inferred from developer OS or CI platform.
5. Existing dual-stack repositories (PLATE itself, adopters that declared Windows support) may keep both .sh and .ps1.
agent_notes: When authoring or modifying scripts: (1) Check if the project explicitly declares Windows support via SPEC.md, .plate config, or bootstrap answers. (2) Default projects (no explicit Windows support) = ship .sh only. (3) Windows-supported (explicit) = ship both .sh (primary) and .ps1 (equivalent behavior). (4) Windows-only (explicit) = .ps1 only. Never infer platform support from developer laptop OS, Windows dependencies, or CI choices. import-payload and bootstrap still install the payload's .ps1 files; tell adopters to delete them unless Windows is declared. Filtering is #1019.
